batchName: Empire: Diocletian and Constantine (AD 284-337) - Latin words
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What was adoratio, which Diocletian demanded?
options: Lying face down before the emperor
questions.explanation: He also wore a gold crown and jewels.
questions.sourceQuote: visitors had to lie face down before him (*adoratio*).

questions.question: What does in hoc signo vinces mean?
questions.explanation: Eusebius said Constantine saw the words with a cross of light above the sun.
questions.sourceQuote: “In this sign, conquer”, usually given in Latin as *in hoc signo vinces*.

questions.question: What was Constantine’s solidus?
options: A gold coin that kept its value for seven centuries
questions.explanation: It kept its weight and purity for seven centuries.
questions.sourceQuote: His new gold coin, the *solidus*, kept its weight and purity for seven centuries.

questions.question: Each diocese was run by a vicarius. What was a vicarius?
questions.explanation: Diocletian grouped nearly a hundred provinces into twelve dioceses.

questions.question: Diocletian taxed land in iuga and people in capita. What were capita?
questions.explanation: A census every five years kept the figures current from 296.

questions.question: What was the labarum?
options: A battle standard bearing the Chi-Rho
questions.explanation: Eusebius said Christ told Constantine in a dream to make it.
questions.sourceQuote: make a battle standard, the *labarum*, bearing the Chi-Rho

questions.question: What was the adventus that Constantine made on 29 October 312?
questions.explanation: Maxentius’s head was paraded through the streets.
questions.sourceQuote: Constantine made a grand entry (*adventus*) into Rome.

questions.question: What was the Edictum de Pretiis Rerum Venalium of 301?
questions.explanation: It set top prices for more than a thousand goods and soon failed.
questions.sourceQuote: his Edict on Maximum Prices (*Edictum de Pretiis Rerum Venalium*)
